title: SOFR Rate Observation — April 16, 2026

source.name: FRED / Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) settled at 3.67% on April 16, 2026, down 5 basis points from the prior day's reading of 3.72%. The rate had been trending upward from 3.61% on April 10 through 3.72% on April 15 before this single-day pullback.
key_points: SOFR closed at 3.67% on April 16, 2026, a 5 bps decline from 3.72% on April 15
The prior week's trend shows SOFR climbing from 3.61% (April 10) to 3.72% (April 15) before today's slight decline
Recent observations: April 13 at 3.63%, April 14 at 3.66%, showing a general upward drift
SOFR is published daily by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York based on overnight repo transactions
why_it_matters: SOFR serves as the primary benchmark for short-term lending and derivatives markets. Movements in this rate signal changes in overnight funding conditions. The recent multi-day climb (3.61% to 3.72%) followed by a 5 bps decline reflects shifting demand for collateralized overnight funding.
macro_context: SOFR movements reflect underlying money market conditions. The recent upward drift from April 10-15 suggests increased demand for overnight funding, while the April 16 decline to 3.67% indicates a partial reversal of that pressure.
market_structure_context: SOFR is calculated from triparty repo transactions cleared through the Fixed Income Clearing Corporation (FICC). It represents the cost of collateralized overnight borrowing and is used as the benchmark for $200+ trillion in financial contracts.
